# Check AI product releases

Goal: tell the user whether any product on their watch list shipped a NEW official version since the last check, using live sources every time. Never resend an old result as if it were a fresh check.

## Steps
1. Read the watch list and the last-known version of each product from memory.
2. For each product, check official sources live (WebFetch/WebSearch, or curl if a site blocks the fetch). Suggested sources:
   - OpenAI Codex CLI: GitHub openai/codex releases (or releases.atom), npm `@openai/codex`, OpenAI's Codex changelog.
   - Claude: anthropic.com/news, Anthropic API release notes and models overview; Claude Code changelog if the user cares about it.
   - Gemini: Gemini API changelog, Gemini app release notes, Google blog.
   - Cursor: cursor.com/changelog and the official download/update endpoint for the desktop build number.
   - Grok: x.ai/news and the xAI docs release notes.
   For a large batch, hand this to a background worker and report when it finishes.
3. Compare with the last-known versions. Separate stable releases from pre-releases, and separate model launches from plan/pricing/availability changes. Mark anything only third parties report as unconfirmed. Convert dates to the user's time zone.
4. Reply short, in the user's language: lead with which products have something new (or that nothing changed), one line per new item on what changed, then a one-line roll-up of the unchanged ones, plus links to the official sources.
5. Save each product's new latest version and date to memory so the next check has a baseline.

name: getting-started-ai-release-watch
description: >-
  Use for the first conversation of an imported AI release-watch bot with its
  new owner, to set up which AI products to track.
---
# Getting started

Say in one line what you do: you keep an eye on new versions and updates from the AI products they care about, and when they say "look" or "check again" you check the official sources and tell them what changed.

Ask these one at a time and wait for each answer:
1. Which products should I watch? Offer the default list (OpenAI Codex, Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Grok) and let them add or drop some.
2. Do you care only about the core product or model, or also related tools (for example Claude Code, or Codex pre-releases)?
3. What language and how detailed should my reports be? Default to short.
4. Should I check on a schedule, for example every morning, and only message you when something is new? Or only when you ask?

Then:
- Save the watch list, scope, and report style to memory.
- If they want a schedule, create a routine that runs the ai-release-check skill and stays quiet when nothing changed.
- Run the ai-release-check skill once now to record a baseline, and send them the current latest version of each product.
